guideTitle: Best Electric Onion and Garlic Choppers (2026)
metaDescription: Seven electric onion and garlic choppers compared: corded 250 W, USB cordless and large dual-bowl models, rated on blades, bowl size, odor control and fit.
expertTake: The Brigii 3-Cup 250W is the best onion and garlic chopper because its corded motor handles whole onions that USB units struggle with, and the press-and-hold design is safe. The 350 ml 4-blade USB-C unit is the value pick for garlic and small jobs. Anyone who chops several onions a week should skip the tiny cordless units and buy a corded mini or a dual-bowl processor. Always match the machine to the onion, not the garlic, since garlic works in anything.
introParagraphs: Onions and garlic are the two foods that most people chop every day, and they are the two that make chopping miserable. Onions make your eyes water and slip under a knife, and garlic leaves a smell on your hands and the board. A small electric chopper takes both jobs away in a few seconds.

The catch is that onions and garlic behave differently. Garlic is small and soft and suits almost any mincer, while onions are large, wet and layered and need real torque to chop evenly. This guide compares seven machines on that difference, looking at motor type, blade count, bowl size and odor control from the listing specs. Prices and bundle contents change, so confirm exactly what is in the box on the listing before you order.

products.name: Brigii 3-Cup Electric Garlic Mincer and Onion Chopper 250W

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Press and hold the top button

products.description:
The Brigii is the one machine here that is clearly built for onions as well as garlic. A 250 watt corded motor drives S-shaped double-layer oblique blades, and the listing says it chops ingredients in 3 to 10 seconds and is four times as powerful as USB-rechargeable choppers. Press-and-hold control means the blades stop when you release the button.

A wall outlet is required, and it is bigger than the pocket-size USB units. Three cups is a good size for one large onion or several cloves, but not for a big batch for a crowd. Compared with the 350 ml cordless units it has far more torque, and compared with the dual-bowl KOIOS it is simpler and smaller.

Quarter the onion, add it in two loads rather than overfilling and pulse by pressing and releasing. Onion residue dries into a hard film, so rinse the bowl and lid right after use. Daily onion chopping calls for a dependable corded machine, and this is one. Because the blades are oblique, they pull food down toward the cutting edge, which is why the chop looks more even than in flat-blade minis.
products.bestFor: Cooks who chop whole onions and garlic every day.
pros: 250 watt corded motor handles whole onions

products.name: KOIOS 500W Electric Food Chopper with Two 8 Cup Bowls
products.description:
The KOIOS is the batch machine. A 500 watt pure copper motor and S-shaped bi-level blades chop several onions at once, and two 8 cup bowls let you handle two foods without mixing flavors. If you prep a week of onions and garlic for the freezer, this is the right size.

The tradeoff is bulk. Eight cup bowls are large and take space, and the machine is overkill for a clove or two. Compared with the Brigii it handles far more, but cleaning two bowls and blades takes longer. The two speeds help you choose a coarse or fine chop.

Cut onions into quarters, process in two loads and pulse to avoid mush. Wash the bowls promptly. It suits meal preppers who chop large amounts of aromatics at once. With that much strength, it can also grind nuts and bread crumbs when the onions are done.
products.bestFor: Meal preppers who chop several onions at a time.
pros: Two 8 cup bowls keep flavors separate
cons: Overkill for a clove of garlic

products.name: 5-in-1 Wireless Electric Vegetable Chopper and Food Processor
products.description:
This wireless unit combines chopping, slicing, grating and peeling, and has a large round feeding port. For onions and garlic it chops, but its range is wider, so it can also slice onions for stir-fries and grate vegetables. The wireless design avoids a cord near the sink.

Brand recognition is low, and the power matches that. A battery motor limits how much it can chop per charge, and it is unbranded, so support is uncertain. Compared with the Brigii it is more versatile but less powerful for whole onions.

Charge before use, wash the parts by hand and keep water out of the motor head. One wireless tool covers several vegetable jobs. Because the port is wide, you can drop in a peeled shallot or a small onion without quartering it first.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want slicing and grating as well as chopping.

products.name: 350 ml USB-C Rechargeable Mini Veggie Chopper with 4 Blades
products.description:
This compact unit has four sharp 304 stainless steel blades at staggered angles, a 350 ml bowl and USB-C charging. At 3.94 by 4.53 inches it fits in a drawer, and the built-in battery means no cord. For garlic, ginger, chili and half an onion it is a convenient little tool.

The tradeoff is torque. A small battery motor is best for soft foods, and a whole onion needs to be quartered and processed in two rounds. No brand name is attached to it, so read the seller's return policy and warranty terms before you buy. Compared with the Brigii it is more portable but less powerful.

Charge fully, rinse by hand and keep the head dry. It suits garlic-heavy cooks who want a small, cheap tool. Because the battery is small, expect to recharge after a few rounds, so charge it before a big cooking session.
products.bestFor: Garlic and half-onion jobs in a tiny, cord-free tool.

products.name: 320 ml USB-C Vegetable Chopper Garlic Mincer Slicer with 3 Blades

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Press and hold the top button

products.description:
This chopper has three hard, sharp blades and a 320 ml, 1.35 cup bowl sized for small to medium tasks. USB-C charging and press-and-hold control keep it simple. Garlic, onion and similar foods go in, and the blade set is a bit more open than six-blade rivals, which suits chunkier results.

The tradeoff is capacity and torque. A 320 ml bowl handles a small onion, and the motor is not meant for dense foods. It is unbranded. Compared with the 350 ml unit it has fewer blades and a slightly smaller bowl.

Charge before use and hand wash. Its blades give a coarser chop than six-blade units manage. Because the blades are fewer, pulse briefly and check the texture, since it is easy to over-chop soft foods.
products.bestFor: Cooks who like a coarser chop from a small cordless unit.
pros: Three sharp blades give a chunkier chop

products.name: 1.5 Cup 350 ml Electric Garlic Chopper Mini Food Processor
products.description:
This mini food processor has 304 stainless steel blades and a food-grade ABS body, with a one-button control that works once the lid is locked. Garlic and other ingredients are chopped quickly, according to the seller. The lid lock means it will not run unless assembled.

Power is limited and the brand is unknown in this basic small unit. Size and function match the 350 ml four-blade unit, so the choice comes down to price. It is a fine garlic tool.

Wash the bowl promptly after onion. Simplicity and small size are the whole pitch. Because it will not run with the lid off, it is also a reasonable choice for a kitchen with children.
products.bestFor: Garlic and small onion jobs with a lid-lock safety.

products.name: 304 Stainless Portable Cordless Garlic Chopper and Veggie Mincer

specList.label: Control
specList.value: Press and hold the top button

products.description:
This portable mincer has an upgraded high-speed motor, a food-grade PC cup and a 304 stainless steel blade that the listing says has no odor. Press and hold the top button to start and release to stop. It is the simplest and lowest-cost cordless option here.

Power is on the lower side and the brand is not widely known. It is a small battery unit, best for garlic and soft vegetables. Compared with the Brigii it is far weaker, and compared with the other USB units it is simpler.

Charge before use, rinse by hand and keep the head dry. It suits people who want a cheap, portable garlic tool. Light weight makes it easy to pack for camping or travel.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want an inexpensive, portable garlic mincer.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A whole onion is wet and layered, and it resists a weak motor. The Brigii lists 250 watts and the KOIOS 500 watts, while USB units use small batteries. Quarter onions and process in two loads for even results. If you chop onions most days, buy a corded machine rather than a cordless one. A frozen onion is harder on blades, while a chilled one is firmer and sheds fewer vapors, so refrigerate onions before chopping. Avoid chopping very large chunks, and always empty the bowl before adding a second load.

Garlic is small and soft, so even the smallest USB mincer handles it. Peel the cloves first and keep the bowl small so they stay near the blades. The 350 ml and 320 ml units handle a head of garlic easily. For garlic alone, buy the smallest and cheapest unit. If you also grind spices in the same unit, wash it thoroughly between uses so garlic does not flavor your cinnamon.

The Brigii has S-shaped double-layer oblique blades, the 350 ml unit four 304 stainless blades and the 320 ml unit three. More blades give a finer chop faster, while fewer blades leave chunkier pieces. For salsa you want chunkier, for sauces finer. Dull blades bruise onion and release more of the compounds that make you cry, so replace or sharpen when results turn mushy.

The 1.5 cup and 350 ml units suit a few cloves or half an onion, the Brigii three cups suits a large onion and the KOIOS 8 cups suits meal prep. Do not fill past two thirds, since overfilled bowls leave big chunks at the top. Buy for your usual recipe. If you cook for a family, buy a bowl that fits two onions rather than one.

Onion and garlic leave odors in plastic. ABS and PC bowls can hold smell, so rinse right away and wash with a little baking soda. A glass bowl resists odor best. A removable lid seal is worth cleaning because odor collects there. A little white vinegar in warm water also helps remove stubborn smell.

The Brigii, 320 ml unit and portable mincer use press-and-hold control, and the 1.5 cup unit has a lid lock. These stop the blades when you release or when the lid is off. Never reach into a bowl with the motor head attached. Wash blades with a brush, never bare fingers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Onion performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared motor types, favoring corded motors for whole onions. We assumed whole onions need a corded motor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Garlic suitability
howWeEvaluated.description: We confirmed that even small units handle garlic. Garlic is the easy part for any unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared S-shaped, four-blade and three-blade designs. More blades do not equal more power.

howWeEvaluated.title: Odor and cleanup
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed bowl materials and how easy each is to wash. Plastic bowls scored lower for odor retention.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited press-and-hold controls and lid locks. Lid locks scored well.

cards.label: Corded (Brigii, KOIOS)
cards.text: More torque and no charging. Best for onions and daily use.

cards.label: Cordless (USB units)
cards.text: Small, light and portable, but limited by battery. Best for garlic.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded if you chop onions and cordless if you mostly mince garlic. Many cooks keep a corded unit and a small USB unit.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A sealed lid so the onion vapor stays inside, a short chop time and a bowl you can empty away from your face. Chilling the onion for an hour also reduces the vapor.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Brigii chops in 3 to 10 seconds, so you spend less time near the onion.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You chop onions daily or for large batches. A corded Brigii or KOIOS pays back.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly mince garlic. A USB mincer does the job. A second tiny mincer for garlic is cheap.

maintenance.task: Rinse the bowl right after use
maintenance.why: Onion and garlic residue dries into a hard film and leaves odor. Warm water and a drop of soap do most of the work.
Odor collects in the seal and spreads to other foods. A small brush reaches the seal groove.
Water in the head can damage the motor or battery.
Batteries last longer with regular charging. A cable that is not the original may charge more slowly.
Dull blades bruise and release more onion vapor. Replace the blade if available.

faq.q: Can a USB garlic chopper handle onions?
faq.a: Small onions and halves, yes. Whole onions are better in a corded unit like the Brigii. Half onions work well in the 350 ml units.

faq.q: How do I stop my eyes watering?
faq.a: Chop in a closed bowl, chill the onion first and open the lid away from your face. A closed bowl keeps most vapors inside.

faq.q: How do I get rid of the garlic smell?
faq.a: Rinse promptly and wash with a little baking soda. A glass bowl resists odor best.

faq.q: Do I need to peel garlic?
faq.a: Yes, peel the cloves first. The skins do not chop cleanly and leave bits. Use a small knife to trim the root end first.

faq.q: How full should the bowl be?
faq.a: Fill no more than two thirds, and quarter large onions first. Shake the bowl between pulses to move food.
Check the manual. Hand washing protects the lid seals and is safer for USB units. Never submerge the motor head.
